evidence.quote: The ST samples and ECAP-deformed samples were aged at 510 °C for 10, 30, 60, and 240 min in a tube furnace and air-cooled to room temperature.
After 60 min of aging treatment, small amounts of ω and α phases precipitate in the ST sample.
After 240 min, the ω phase disappears, and a significant content of α phase.
The ST sample is mainly composed of the β phase and a small amount of the quenched martensitic hcp-α’ (002) phase.
The volume fraction of the α′ phase in the ST sample is about 9%
the volume fraction of the SIM α′′ phase in the 1P and 4P samples is about 37% and 32%, respectively.
Moreover, the stress-induced ω phase appears in the twins.
The 2P sample exhibits the maximum volume fraction of the SIM α′′ phase (~51%), and the 3P sample exhibits the maximum volume fraction of twins (~57%).

the lath structure is mainly composed of Σ11-type CSL boundaries and a small number of Σ3-type CSL boundaries. The Σ11-type and Σ3-type CSL boundaries in the metastable β titanium alloy correspond to {332}<113> and {112}〈111〉 twins
the {332}<113> twins gradually transform to {112}〈111〉 twins; thus, the volume fraction of {112}〈111〉 twins gradually increases
the 3P sample exhibits the maximum volume fraction of twins (~57%).

evidence.section: 4.3.2. Effect of ECAP deformation and aging treatment on the elastic modulus
evidence.quote: a high ratio of strength to elastic modulus (~17.15 × 10^3) is obtained.
This indicates that the Ti–Nb alloy is a TWIP/TRIP titanium alloy, and the deformation process simultaneously induces phase transformations and the formation of mechanical twins
